results.comment: 2:50: It is actually incorrect when you say that monthly income dividend does not pay you more. When you are paid monthly, you can re-invest that money each month which would snowball your growth faster if you re-invest those dividends each month (as opposed to quarterly). Whether that company is fundamentally strong is another story but purely from a frequency standpoint, more payments do equal more payment as time goes on (assuming you are re-investing the dividends) but that argument could be said for the same thing if you were re-investing quarterly companies.    This is also why fractional shares are so powerful. It makes your fractional shares squeeze even more juice out of the stock versus having to wait until you have enough for a full share only.   Lets use an example to make it simple If I have 1 stock that is $10 and yields 4%. That means you get $0.10 per quarter. Or I make 0.0033 per month if it pays monthly In a monthly payment, I would have 0.0033c which I can use fractionally shares to buy more shares. Now I own 1.00033 shares of the stock by the next month which means I would receive more dividends, 0.0034c next month. Then next month, I make 0.0035c per month. By the time you receive your quarterly dividend, I already have 0.00035 more of a share than you. These are small numbers because the stock is $10 but if the stock is $50+ and you have $10,000+ in the position, you can see how much more it amplifies. Then you add 5-10 years of compound interest, it will be insane. As you can see, even after 2-3 years, I would be way farther ahead than you in terms of position size.   As I said, this assumes a couple of things. A) You are able to buy fractional shares but assuming you had a large enough position, the fractional shares wouldn't matter. B) The company fundamentally is strong which I agree that finding a strong monthly company is it's own battle.
